The classifier's performance hinges on the quality and distribution of the SATT-3 labeled dataset, which is inherently imbalanced. Focal loss is applied to mitigate the impact of easy examples and focus learning on hard negatives, thereby improving recall and F1 scores. Taguchi L18 augmentation introduces controlled variability in brightness, rotation, and flipping to enhance generalization. The ablation study reveals that brightness variation has the most significant influence on recall, suggesting that visual contrast plays a critical role in detecting risky tackles. The 5-fold cross-validation ensures stable estimates of performance metrics. The derived kernel from Taguchi augmentation defines a probabilistic transformation of input data, enabling GSE to reason about risk transitions under varying environmental conditions.
